I'm 76 this year, and my old man and I have been working these 6 and a half mu for 50 years. With just the two of us, we can't work like the young folks do anymore. I keep about 4 mu for wheat and then maize right after — that's our main food and some cash. The other 2 and a half mu I plant cotton, which gives us extra money but kills my back at picking time.

For the wheat, I plant around October 10th, same as my whole life. I use the seed I saved from last year — no need to buy. Before planting, I put down two bags of compound fertilizer on the 4 mu, that's about 50 jin per mu. Then at jointing, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I topdress with two bags of urea, about 40 jin per mu total. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping water costs electricity money, so I don't waste it, but you can't skip grain filling or the grains will be shriveled and small. I spray herbicide once after planting. For harvest, my nephew brings his combine for two days — costs money but saves our backs. I expect about 380 jin per mu if the weather is fair. Last year I got around 360, so I'm hoping for a bit better.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 12th. There's no time to plow — I just plant into the wheat stubble with the seeder. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 75 yuan per mu. I put down one bag of compound and one and a half bags of urea on the 4 mu at planting time. I irrigate twice if July is dry. One spray of herbicide. I expect 450 jin per mu, maybe 500 if it rains well.

Cotton I plant in mid-April. I use local seed, about 35 yuan per mu for the treated seed. Half a bag of compound for the 2 and a half mu, and half a bag of urea at flowering. Irrigate twice — once at planting if dry, once at boll stage. Cotton needs insecticide for bollworm, I spray twice. The picking is the hard part — at my age I can only do a little every day, bending down hurts my waist. I expect about 220 jin of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer got expensive this year, so I'm using a bit less than some folks recommend, but not too little — I'd rather waste a bit of money than risk losing the crop. We need the grain to eat and some to sell for cash. Cash is tight with just us two, so I buy inputs little by little and don't hire labor except for the wheat combine.
